scope: Primary-source-verified PC or desktop game source ports and reimplementations targeting consoles, plus console-target builds not represented in the live catalog. These are candidate imports only; SQLite and generated docs were not changed.

projects.title: OpenMW PlayStation Vita Port
projects.platform: Windows PC game data / OpenMW engine → PlayStation Vita
projects.status: The repository documents an installable Vita VPK, touch/controller mappings, mod and save paths, and VitaSDK build commands. Morrowind data files must be supplied by the player. The README does not claim a complete-game hardware test.
projects.summary: Community Vita port of OpenMW, the open-source Morrowind engine reimplementation. It adapts rendering, controls, memory management, and settings to the Vita and supports saves shared with desktop OpenMW.
projects.strategy: Port the OpenMW C++ engine to VitaSDK with Vita-specific rendering, controls, and memory optimizations
projects.source_available: Public source repository; the player must provide legally obtained Morrowind game data

sources.label: Maintainer README: Vita installation, controls, data requirements, saves, and build instructions
Upstream OpenMW engine source and project

projects.title: vitaQuake
projects.platform: Quake WinQuake source and game data → PlayStation Vita
projects.status: The maintainer describes vitaQuake as a Quake engine source port for PS Vita. The README documents support for Quake's official mission packs and lists mod compatibility per title; it does not claim full campaign completion. Game data is supplied separately.
projects.summary: Native PlayStation Vita adaptation of the WinQuake codebase, with Vita-specific controls, audio tracks, expansion and mod support.
projects.strategy: Port WinQuake source to the Vita SDK and adapt rendering, input, and audio to Vita hardware
projects.source_available: Public source repository; original Quake or shareware data is required separately

sources.label: Maintainer README: source-port scope, expansion support, and per-mod compatibility notes
Maintainer release page

projects.title: ioQuake3-U
projects.game: Quake III Arena and compatible id Tech 3 games
projects.platform: Windows/Linux id Tech 3 source and game data → Nintendo Wii U
projects.status: The maintainer reports that it boots, loads maps, and plays with bots using native GX2 rendering. The Wii U build tree produces separate Quake III Arena, Team Arena, OpenArena, Quake3Classic, and Elite Force flavors. Original game data is required; no full-campaign result is claimed.
projects.summary: Native Wii U port of ioQuake3 with a GX2 graphics backend, Wii U controller support, and five id Tech 3-compatible build flavors.
projects.strategy: Port ioQuake3 to Wii U using devkitPPC/wut and a native GX2 renderer, retaining the shared engine/game code
projects.source_available: Public source repository; user-supplied data for a compatible id Tech 3 game is required
projects.subtype: Wii U native homebrew; multi-title engine port

sources.label: Maintainer README: tested status, target flavors, controller support, and build commands
Wii U port installation and game-data requirements

projects.title: SDLPoP Vita Enhanced
projects.platform: DOS PC disassembly → SDLPoP reimplementation → PlayStation Vita
projects.status: The repository documents a Vita VPK build and VitaSDK installation. Original game data must be supplied separately; music is disabled by default on Vita. The README does not state a complete-game test result.
projects.summary: Enhanced PS Vita port of SDLPoP, an open-source Prince of Persia implementation based on the DOS game disassembly. Vita-specific configuration covers the game dataset, palette, and controls.
projects.strategy: Port SDLPoP's C implementation to VitaSDK and add Vita display, input, and dataset options
projects.source_available: Public source repository and Vita build instructions; original Prince of Persia data files are not included

sources.label: Maintainer README: DOS disassembly lineage, Vita installation, data requirements, and build commands

projects.title: SDLPoP Dreamcast Port
projects.platform: DOS PC disassembly → SDLPoP reimplementation → Sega Dreamcast
projects.status: The repository contains a Dreamcast/KallistiOS build recipe and SDL2 Dreamcast setup steps. It identifies itself as an open-source port based on the DOS disassembly; the README does not give a real-hardware test or full-game result.
projects.summary: Sega Dreamcast port of SDLPoP, the Prince of Persia implementation based on the original DOS disassembly, with Dreamcast build support and additional project-specific features.
projects.strategy: Adapt the SDLPoP source to SDL2 and KallistiOS for a native Dreamcast build

projects.title: Celeste Classic Dreamcast Port (ccleste-dreamcast)
projects.platform: PICO-8 game → portable C source port → Sega Dreamcast
projects.status: The public repository contains Dreamcast-specific SDL/build files and instructions for producing a CDI with KallistiOS. The README notes occasional sound crackling; it does not claim full-game hardware validation.
projects.summary: Sega Dreamcast target for ccleste, a portable C source port of the PICO-8 Celeste Classic game. The port uses KallistiOS and SDL-based Dreamcast components.
projects.strategy: Adapt the portable ccleste C game code and SDL audio/video/input layers to KallistiOS, then package a Dreamcast disc image
projects.source_available: Public source repository; README identifies the original PICO-8 game but does not establish whether all original game data is included

projects.title: OpenLara Console Ports
projects.platform: Classic Tomb Raider data / OpenLara engine → Nintendo 3DS, PlayStation Vita, PSP, Nintendo Switch, Original Xbox, Xbox One, and other listed platforms
projects.status: The upstream repository contains console-specific code and release entries for 3DS, Vita, PSP, Switch, Original Xbox, and Xbox One. The latest release notes list these console target builds as last updated between 2020 and 2021; the Switch entry is marked pre-release and PSP alpha. Those dates describe target artifacts, not current hardware testing.

projects.strategy: Reimplement the classic Tomb Raider engine in portable C++ and provide platform-specific rendering, input, and packaging backends

projects.strategy: Adapt released Quake C source to KallistiOS and the Dreamcast SH-4, with software and GL rendering builds
projects.source_available: Public source-code backup; Quake shareware or commercial data files are required separately

projects.summary: Historical Sega Dreamcast port of the released Quake II source code (DCQ2), with a software renderer, controller support, and VMU save support documented by the maintainer.
projects.strategy: Adapt the released Quake II C code to KallistiOS and Dreamcast hardware; retain a software rendering path to fit the target

projects.title: Trogdor: Reburninated
projects.platform: Adobe Flash / ActionScript game → manually rewritten C++ recreation for PC, Android, Nintendo Switch, Wii U, Wii, GameCube, 3DS, PlayStation Vita, PSP, PortMaster, and FunKey
projects.status: The maintainer reports playable builds for PC, Android, and the listed homebrew platforms. The README describes a manual ActionScript-to-C++ recreation from Flash-decompiled code and ported assets, but does not give platform-by-platform version or hardware test details.
projects.summary: Enhanced, open-source recreation of the Homestar Runner Flash game Trogdor. It ports the original ActionScript logic and assets into C++ and adds configurable difficulty, saves, level selection, and other features.
projects.strategy: Manually rewrite decompiled ActionScript game logic in C++ and adapt the SDL-based recreation to console and handheld homebrew targets
projects.source_available: Public MIT-licensed source repository; the README states that original Homestar Runner rights remain with their owners
